subject: social-studies
title: Neighbourhood Change: One Site, Stage by Stage

slides.heading: Neighbourhood Change: One Site, Stage by Stage
bullets: How one neighbourhood site changes stage by stage: a few low-rise houses on open ground first, transport links arriving next as an MRT station and bus stop open, housing blocks then rising plot by plot, and shops, a market and a school opening as families move in, with the population bar climbing at every stage
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we watch one site in a neighbourhood change stage by stage, and we keep asking what arrived at each stage and why it came in that order.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Explain how a neighbourhood changes in stages: low-rise houses and open ground, transport links arriving first, housing blocks rising plot by plot, shops, a market and a school opening as families move in
Name what happens at each stage and why the population bar climbs at every stage
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to tell the whole story of the site in the right order.

slides.heading: The old photograph and the new photograph look like different places - did it all change overnight?
bullets: Before-and-after photographs of a neighbourhood look completely different
Did the flats, shops and MRT station all appear in a single step, or is there a stage-by-stage story in between?
slides.notes: Ask the class: when two photographs look totally different, does that mean everything changed at once? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the animation replays the change one stage at a time.

slides.heading: Transport arrives before homes - change happens stage by stage
bullets: A neighbourhood changes stage by stage: transport links arrive first, so the site is easy to reach before many people live there
Housing blocks rise plot by plot, and only as families move in do the shops, market and school open - the population grows at every stage, not in one jump
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: the order matters - transport first, then homes, then the shops, market and school that serve the families who moved in.

slides.heading: Stage 1: the site as found - houses and open ground
bullets: At the start the site is a quiet corner of the neighbourhood: a few low-rise houses stand on open ground
Only a few families live here, so the population bar is at its lowest
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the low-rise houses, the open ground and the low population bar: this is the site as found, before any change.

slides.heading: Stage 2: transport arrives first - MRT station and bus stop
bullets: The first change is transport: an MRT station and a bus stop arrive, so the site is easy to reach
More people can now live and travel here, and the population bar climbs one step
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and follow the new station and bus stop: transport arrives first, before the housing blocks, and the bar climbs one step.

slides.heading: Stage 3: blocks rise, then shops, a market and a school open
bullets: Housing blocks rise plot by plot on the open ground, and as families move into the flats, shops, a market and a school open to serve them
The population bar climbs again as more families move in
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and pause as each plot is built: blocks first, then the shops, market and school that open because families now live here.

slides.heading: Stage 4: the wrong turn, corrected - change happens stage by stage
bullets: The all-at-once shortcut is played out - everything flashes in together - and then corrected
The true sequence is replayed: transport first, blocks plot by plot, then shops, market and school as families arrive, with the population bar climbing at every stage
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and contrast the two versions: the shortcut puts everything in a single step, the real change runs stage by stage in order.

slides.heading: Worked example: following one site from open ground to a busy neighbourhood
bullets: Start: a few low-rise houses on open ground, with only a few families living here
Finish: a busy neighbourhood of flats, shops, a market and a school - reached only stage by stage, transport first, as the population bar climbs at every stage
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Stage 1, low-rise houses and open ground. Stage 2, transport arrives first - MRT station and bus stop. Stage 3, housing blocks rise plot by plot and shops, a market and a school open as families move in. Stage 4, the all-at-once wrong turn is corrected. At each stage ask: what arrived here, and did the population bar climb?

slides.heading: Your turn: run the stages in order
bullets: In pairs: starting from the site as found, name each stage in order and say what arrived at that stage and what happened to the population bar
Then swap and check: did your partner bring transport in first and let families move in before the shops and school opened, or did everything appear at once?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for all four stages in order, then take two pairs answers: houses and open ground, transport first, blocks plot by plot, shops, market and school as families move in.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says a neighbourhood changes all at once
Name the stages in order - transport first, blocks plot by plot, shops and school as families move in - to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers keep the stages apart and run them in the right order.
